pred_ddx.label: Mucinous cystic neoplasm of the pancreas

Mucinous cystic neoplasm of the pancreas: The large size of the cystic mass, its location in the pancreatic head, and the patient's symptoms suggest a mucinous cystic neoplasm as a likely diagnosis, given the absence of invasion, lymphadenopathy, and normal CA 19-9 level.
Serous cystadenoma of the pancreas: The well-circumscribed nature of the cystic mass and its location in the pancreatic head, combined with the patient's symptoms and the lack of elevated CA 19-9, make serous cystadenoma a plausible diagnosis, although further evaluation is needed to differentiate it from other cystic neoplasms.
